text.p: THE AUSTRALIAN FINANCIAL REVIEW

News Corp and Telstra will move quickly to merge their pay-TV venture Foxtel with the ailing Australis Media in order to exploit their new relationship with Kerry Packer's Publishing and Broadcasting Ltd. An Optus source described the move as the first step in the rationalisation of the pay-TV industry. Page 1.

The Australian Wheat Board has warned the international grain market that its current forecast for another big wheat harvest this summer is looking vulnerable due to the effect of El Nino which gave Australia a deteriorating weather outlook. Page 3.

Singapore Airlines is expected to push hard for a stake in Air New Zealand Ltd as their tripartite alliance with the Ansett group takes shape in the next few months. SIA could emerge with substantial shareholdings in both Air New Zealand and Ansett to underpin their commercial deal announced last Friday. Page 23.

An independent report by Grant Samuel and Associates has found Foster's Brewing Group's A$625 million share buyback is expected to reduce the company's 1996-97 earnings by A$30.6 million because of higher interest costs. Page 24

Former New South Wales Treasury Corp chief economist and now AUSBIL Partners associate director of fixed investment John Honan has warned fund managers and superannuation fund trustees will inevitably expose investors to greater risk unless they quickly aquire the skills needed to assess the range of new investment opportunities. Page 27.

QNI managing director Wyn Davies has defended his company's planned merger with South Africa-based miner Gencor Ltd's nickel business against criticism the A$2.3 billion deal short-changes shareholders. QNI shares have traded lower since the deal was annonced last week. Page 28.
THE AUSTRALIAN

BHP is one of several companies to have received permission to assess confidential information about United States energy group Conoco's proposal for a A$1.8 billion coal seam methane for the Bowen Basin in Queensland, with the potential to become a partner. Page 29.

United States-based investment firm HVP Partners managing director Philip Bilden said yesterday that offshore venture capital companies were avoiding Australia because of inconsistent capital gains tax laws, costing Australia hundreds of millions of dollas in potential investment capital. Page 29.

Parties opposing Westpac's proposed takeover of the Bank of Melbourne are devising alternative strategies to block the merger if the Australian Competition and Consumer Commission approves the A$1.4 billion bid. The Australian Consumers Association has been scrutinising the rules relating to the approval process by BML customers. Page 29.

Paul Thompson's DMG Radio Australia is planning more acquisitions in regional and metropolitan radio to expand on the 20 stations it has acquired since entering the Australian radio arena 16 months ago. DMG is unlikely to release financial results for the 1997 September year but is profitable and budgeting for strong growth in the next year. Page 31.

The Colonial State Bank has launched a retirement savings account, marking the first direct entry by a bank into the hotly contested superannuation market. Other banks are expected to follow shortly, after final preparations to meet the 1 July launch date RSAs will be a simple way to begin saving for superannuation, particularly for people in irregular employment. Page 31.

Limited supplies, widespread demand and the weaker dollar have pushed Australian wool prices to their highest level in two seasons. BWK Australasia associate director Michael Avery said the market had been dominated by low supply, and significantly stonger Chinese buying in the past couple of weeks had fuelled the market. Page 31.
THE SYDNEY MORNING HERALD

The Australian Competition and Consumer Commission has warned big pay-TV losses would not necessarily mean approval for a merger between two of Australia's three operators, as Foxtel steps up its plans to merge with Australis. The ACCC blocked the takeover of Australis by Foxtel in 1995 due to concerns it would limit competition. Page 37.

Westpac Banking Corporation's share of the banks' national home lending market has slumped from 18.5 per cent to 17 per cent in one year, as its home loan book shrank by about A$200 million to A$22.7 billion, despite a A$400 million investment in a high-tech mortgage processing centre and numerous awards for its mortgage products. Page 37.

In a push to make Foxtel a more profitable project, News Corporation and Telstra's joint pay-TV venture Foxtel will issue an ultimatum to satellite pay-TV operator Australis Media to merge or face the possibility of a financial crisis before the end of ths year. Page 37.

National Australia Asset Management's strategy to double its size by the end of the century will almost certainly include an acquisition. NAAM managing director Paul Laband said several potential targets had been identified in the domestic market, but the fund manager was not considering anything now. Page 39.

In a move that will push Australia a step closer towards full ATM interchange, Westpac will link its network with Bank of Melbourne, Credit Union Settlement Services and Colonial State Bank, giving Westpac customers access to more than 6000 ATMs - more thn 85 per cent of Australia's network. Page 39.

The New South Wales Government has passed legislation that should close a loophole allowing companies to avoid stamp duty through takeovers done via a scheme of arrangement instead of by buying all the target's shares, as has been the case in some of the biggest corporate mergers in recent years. Page 39.
THE AGE

Foxtel will deliver an ultimatum to Australis to merge or face the possibility of a financial crisis by the end of the year. It is believed Optus will step up plans to merge with the satellite pay-TV operator, after the Australian Competition and Consumer Commission blocked a 1995 merger attempt as anti-competitive. Page B1.

The Australian Competition and Consumer Commission says its response to Westpac's A$1.44 billion bid for Bank of Melbourne will probably be released on Thursday or Friday. BML's share price has recovered from early June, when market speculation suggested he ACCC would oppose the takeover. Page B3.

Following an earlier agreement linking Westpac automatic teller machines with the ANZ-NAB alliance, Westpac will link its ATM network with Bank of Melbourne, Credit Union Settlement Services and Colonial State Australia. Page B3.

Foster's Brewing Group's proposed A$625 million share buyback has few identifiable drawbacks according to an independent report by Grant Samuel and Associates. Although Foster's gearing will rise to about 70 per cent from 35 per cent as new debt is used t finance the purchase, this was still "within prudent limits". Page B3.

The Australian Wheat Board has described as premature the Australian Bureau of Agricultural and Resource Economics forecasts that the recurrence of the El Nino weather pattern would cause up to a 30 per cent drop in wheat crops. Page B2.

Geoffrey Thompson Holdings group, a publicly-listed fruit packing and distribution company, will hold a meeting of shareholders today to discuss a pivotal decision to expand the group's board of directors. Some shareholders are concerned the move would mean a radical shift in control for the group. Page B2.
-- Reuters Sydney Newsroom 61-2 9373-1800
